questions.prompt: What's on our call wrap-up checklist?

options.text: Quote pricing, recap features, book the AE, send the contract
Confirm budget, decision maker, timeline and the need again
Send the link, end the call quickly, log it, move on to the next
Ask for acceptance, recap the time, set follow-up, name the topic

questions.source: Day 8, "Finish the call strong"

questions.prompt: How far out should you aim to book a demo?

options.text: About a week out
Within two weeks
0–3 days out
Whatever they pick first

questions.source: Day 8, "Book it close"

questions.prompt: The owner says: "Sure, send me something." Is that a confirmed meeting?

options.text: Yes: send the invite and it counts as booked
No: it needs a named time and an accepted invite
Yes, as long as you log it as a Meeting Set
No: you need her budget first before it counts

questions.reveal: A calendar invite is a record of an intention. A confirmed meeting is a time they named and an invite they accepted.
questions.source: Day 8, "Make it real while you still have them"

questions.prompt: You just got the yes. What do you do first?

options.text: Say back why she agreed, in her words
Thank her and get off the call quickly
Pitch two more features while she's warm
Ask whether she's talked to other vendors

questions.source: Day 8, "Finish the call strong"

questions.prompt: She can only meet in ten days. What do you do?

options.text: Refuse, since past three days it won't hold
Book it, and skip reminders until it's close
Tell her to call you when her schedule clears
Book it, and plan extra protection for it

questions.reveal: Book what they'll take, but treat it as a meeting that needs more protection. Interest, context and memory all fade while you wait.
questions.source: Day 8, "Book it close" (facilitator note)

questions.prompt: Which line asks for the acceptance the way Day 8 teaches?

options.text: Accept it whenever you get a chance, there's honestly no rush at all.
You'll get an invite from us at some point, so keep an eye out.
I just sent the invite. Can you click Yes so it's on your calendar?
I'll just assume you're coming unless I hear otherwise from you.

options.text: Your manager, just in case
You, the SDR who booked it
The AE's team lead, for cover
No one else needs to be on it

questions.prompt: Why say "If it's not accepted by 3, I'll give you a call" on the booking call?

options.text: It gives you a non-pushy reason to call back
It puts pressure on her to decide on the spot
It's required for the meeting to count at all
It means you can skip the day-before call

options.text: In SDR Additional Notes on the contact record
In the description of the calendar invite
In a direct Slack message sent to the AE
Logged via the Playbook, pinned to the company

Who they are, why they agreed, what matters, relevant context

Their name, their title, their email, their phone number

options.text: The problem in her words: chasing late payments
Payroll, since that's what she asked about
Both, listed as features she wants to see
Neither, since the AE will find out in discovery

questions.prompt: You join the demo you booked. What's your role once the prospect is on?

options.text: Run the first part of discovery yourself, then hand it over
Stay on mute and watch the whole demo from start to finish
Re-pitch why Momence is a fit before the AE starts
Introduce her, give a 30–60 second handoff, then let the AE lead

questions.prompt: A few minutes in, the prospect hasn't joined. What do you do?

options.text: Wait the full 30 minutes in case she's just late
Leave the call and let the AE deal with her
Call and help her into the meeting already running
Email her a link to reschedule for next week

questions.reveal: If you're on the call, you know right away. The goal is to turn a no-show into a live conversation while it's still fresh.

questions.prompt: Besides confirming the time, what does the intro email do?

options.text: Shares pricing so there are no surprises on the call
Introduces the AE by name and puts them on the thread
Lists every feature the AE is planning to show
Asks the prospect to fill in a short survey first

questions.source: Day 8, "The AE should not walk in blind" (facilitator note)

questions.prompt: Piper's note says the prospect is "excited and ready to switch." On the call she said she's "just looking." What do you do?

options.text: Change it to match what she actually said
Leave it, since it helps the AE get ready
Delete the whole note and write it from scratch
Add that she'll probably switch after the demo

questions.reveal: The AE plans the demo around your note. Make the prospect sound exactly as interested as she was, no more.

questions.prompt: What does an accepted invite tell you?

options.text: The meeting is certain, so you can stop
She's already decided to buy Momence
Nothing, since most people accept by reflex
She engaged with it, but it's not a guarantee

questions.prompt: It's the day before and the invite still isn't accepted. What's your first move?

options.text: Cancel it and book a new time instead
Leave it, since acceptance isn't required
Call to check it arrived, then text or email
Ask the AE to follow up with her directly

questions.source: Day 8, "Follow-up should reduce friction"; handbook, Protect the Meeting

questions.prompt: If the invite is still unaccepted the day before, what does our cadence call for?

options.text: One short email the morning of the demo, and nothing else
Two or three calls, a final message, then a text or email
Five calls in a row until she finally picks up
A text every couple of hours until she replies

questions.source: Day 8, "Follow-up should reduce friction"

questions.prompt: It's the morning of the demo and she picks up. What do you do?

options.text: Confirm, text the Zoom link and suggest a laptop
Ask whether she'd rather move it to another day
Re-pitch why the demo is worth her time today
Remind her that she promised she'd show up

questions.source: Day 8, "Follow-up should reduce friction"

questions.prompt: Which line is assumptive, not aggressive?

options.text: Just checking you're still okay to meet, or should we move it?
You committed to this, so I'll expect you there at 10 sharp.
No pressure at all if today doesn't really work anymore.
Looking forward to 10 today. I'll text you the Zoom link now.

questions.reveal: Talk as though the meeting is happening and don't volunteer a reschedule. Still leave the door open for them to tell you if something changed.

questions.prompt: A teammate says confirmation calls feel like bothering people. What's the best response?

options.text: Then skip them for prospects who sounded keen on the call.
Only follow up when the AE asks you to confirm the demo.
You said you'd check in on the call. This is keeping your word.
Send emails instead, since they're less intrusive than calls.

The SDR who booked it

questions.prompt: She cancels: "Something came up this week." What do you do?

options.text: Set a task to call her next month
Reschedule fast, while it's still fresh
Log Not Interested and let it cool off
Wait for her to reach back out to you

options.text: Call, not email, to find out the real reason
Email her a link to pick a new time
Log it Dead and move on right away
Send the AE's calendar so she can choose

questions.prompt: She says: "Talk to me in two months, we're opening a second location." What do you do?

options.text: Book a demo two months out right now, just in case
Keep calling weekly so she doesn't forget about you
Mark it Dead until she gets back in touch
Check it's real, then log the timing and set a task

options.text: Cancellations, not no-shows
No-shows, not cancellations

Neither, it's up to the SDR

questions.source: Handbook, Handle a Cancelled Demo

questions.prompt: After a "leave me alone" cancel, what's the question to ask yourself?

options.text: Was the booking call really a yes?
Did I send enough reminder emails?
Was the AE the right fit for her?
Should I have offered her a discount?

questions.reveal: A soft yes taken on the cold call shows up later as a cancel or a no-show. The fix is on the booking call, not in the follow-up.
